milestones.title: Kickoff: scope locked, owners named, tier agreed
Feature freeze: nothing new merges to the release branch
Positioning locked; docs plan and migration guide outlined
API/string freeze; translation and docs handoff
Public beta / RC1 cut and announced to early adopters
Code freeze: release-blocking fixes only, each with a written justification
Release notes, announcement post and social kit drafted
Licence/IP review and security review complete; embargoed advisories staged
Docs complete: migration guide, upgrade path, reference regenerated
Final RC; support runbook and triage rota published
Embargoed briefings to press, sponsors, downstream maintainers
Full release dry run: build, sign, publish to a staging channel, install from it
Go/no-go #1: every blocking gate green or explicitly waived
Final go/no-go; artifacts staged, posts queued, rollback rehearsed
Launch day: publish, announce, staff the thread
First 72 hours: triage rota live, hotfix branch ready

gates.title: Scope locked: shipped feature list matches the plan
gates.note: GitHub release tracker #5844 links Beta 0, Beta 1, Beta 2, Beta 3, RC1, and GA milestones aligned to this record. Final scope approval remains open.

gates.title: Version number matches the change set (major iff breaking)
gates.note: v3.0.0-beta.0 through beta.8 were published from master; beta.8 was published at 2026-08-12T08:20:32Z by successful Nightly Release v3 run 31577849776. The beta.8 tag still contains runtime package metadata versioned 3.0.0-beta.7, while npm publication run 31583811321 later published @wailsio/runtime 3.0.0-beta.8 from post-tag master; PR #5959 proposes future lockstep but is not merged. Maintainer direction recorded in #5876 and implemented by merged PR #5946 defines the current v3 release as a source tag/GitHub prerelease with CLI installation through go install, without attached desktop binaries. This evidence ledger remains at its beta.0 path, and release-stage/version approval is not recorded, so this gate remains open.

gates.title: Compatibility promise stated: supported platforms, runtimes, minimum versions
gates.note: Desktop compatibility promise is now stated in docs/src/content/docs/status.mdx: Windows 10/11 amd64/arm64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, Linux amd64/arm64 with GTK4 default and GTK3 legacy through v3.0.x, Go 1.25+, and experimental mobile. Maintainer approval remains required.

gates.title: Deprecations announced with a removal version; scheduled removals actually removed
Upgrade path tested from the last two releases on real projects
Rollback/downgrade path documented and rehearsed
Artifacts build reproducibly for every published platform
gates.note: Historical Release v3 runs 30747695287 (beta.0) and 30748402783 (beta.1) published six desktop binaries plus SHA256SUMS. Beta.2 through beta.8 have zero attached assets. Before the tag-only decision was implemented, beta.3 through beta.7 Release v3 runs built the desktop set and failed to attach it to immutable releases; beta.6 run 31320435426 and beta.7 run 31506762359 are the latest examples, with beta.7 generating six binaries, SHA256SUMS, and provenance before HTTP 422. Maintainer direction in #5876 made zero-asset tag-only releases intentional, merged PR #5946 removed release-v3.yml plus its nightly dispatch, and successful run 31577849776 published beta.8 by the tag-only path. The artifact gate has not been explicitly redefined, passed, or waived for this policy, so it remains open.

gates.title: Artifacts signed; checksums and provenance published
gates.note: The beta.1 tag-triggered run 30748399250 failed because Apple signing credentials were absent; run 30748402783 then published unsigned macOS binaries after signing/notarization was removed. Maintainer direction in #5876 now makes v3 releases tag-only, and merged PR #5946 removed the desktop-binary workflow, so platform binary signing is not part of the current publication path. No explicit evidence redefines, passes, or waives this signing gate for source-tag distribution, so it remains open.

gates.title: Install verified from the published channel, not the build dir
gates.note: Maintainer direction in #5876 identifies `go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@latest` as the current published CLI channel, and merged PR #5946 removes the unused desktop-binary publication path. Beta.8 was published at 2026-08-12T08:20:32Z, but no clean-machine installation and version check from beta.8 or `@latest` is recorded in this ledger. The channel is now identified, but installation evidence is still absent, so this gate remains open.

gates.note: Beta.7 published as a zero-asset prerelease at 2026-08-11T15:23:34Z. The still-present desktop workflow then ran as 31506762359, built six binaries plus SHA256SUMS and provenance, and failed HTTP 422 against the immutable release. Maintainer direction in #5876 made that workflow obsolete, and merged PR #5946 removed release-v3.yml and its nightly dispatch. Successful Nightly Release v3 run 31577849776 then published beta.8 at 2026-08-12T08:20:32Z through the intended tag-only path. README.md and comms/launch-sequence.md now describe the tag-only/go-install path, but named owners, a completed rehearsal, and final approval are not recorded, so this gate remains open.

gates.title: Support rota staffed for the first 72 hours
Hotfix path rehearsed: branch, build, publish within one working day
gates.note: The current tag-only policy removes binary-asset recovery from the hotfix path. GitHub releases and Go module versions remain immutable once consumed, so recovery should use a new semver tag rather than replace a published version. Merged PR #5946 removed the obsolete asset workflow, but no end-to-end tag-only hotfix rehearsal or timed evidence is recorded. This gate remains open.
